He made them like an adjective (naʿt) of a definite noun, though they are indefinite; do you not see that you say: marartu bi-rajulin shadīdi al-qalbi ("I passed by a man strong of heart")? Except that together with them came His words ﴿ذى الطول﴾, which is definite, so they were made to run in its course. Their genitive may also be by repetition (takrīr, i.e. as a badal (substitute)), in which case definite and indefinite are the same. Similar are His words: ﴿وَهُوَ الْغَفُورُ الوَدُودُ، ذُو العرشِ المجيدُ، فعَّالٌ لما يريدُ﴾: this is by repetition, [163/ا] because faʿʿāl is purely indefinite. Similar are His words: ﴿رفيعُ الدرجاتِ ذو العرشِ﴾: rafīʿ is indefinite, and it was made to run as a fresh start (istiʾnāf), or on the explanation of the first case.

farraa:5-5.t:
His words: ﴿وَهَمَّتْ كُـلُّ أُمَّةٍ بِرَسُولِهِمْ﴾.
He referred it to the men. In the reading (ḥarf) of ʿAbdallāh it is "bi-rasūlihā" ("its messenger"), and all is correct.

farraa:8-8.t:
His words: ﴿وَأَدْخِلْهُمْ جَنَّاتِ عَدْنٍ﴾.
Some read "jannata ʿadnin" in the singular, and so it is in the reading of ʿAbdallāh: singular.
His words: ﴿وَمَن صَـلَحَ مِنْ آبَآئِهِمْ﴾.
man is accusative from two possible places: if you wish you may make (wa-man) refer back to the hāʾ and mīm in "wa-adkhilhum", and if you wish to the hāʾ and mīm in "waʿadtahum".

farraa:10-10.t:
His words: ﴿يُنَادَوْنَ لَمَقْتُ ٱللَّهِ﴾.
The meaning in it is: they will be called out to that Allah's loathing of you is greater than your loathing of yourselves on the Day of Resurrection; for they loathed themselves since they had abandoned faith. But the lām suffices instead of saying, in speech: nādaytu anna Zaydan qāʾimun ("I proclaimed that Zayd is standing"), and nādaytu la-Zaydun qāʾimun. Similar is: ﴿ثم بَدا لهم من بعدِ ما رَأوا الآياتِ﴾ (the verse). The lām is equivalent to anna in every expression resembling "saying", such as "they are called out to", "they are told", and the like.

farraa:15-15.t:
His words: ﴿يُلْقِي ٱلرُّوحَ مِنْ أَمْرِهِ عَلَىٰ مَن يَشَآءُ مِنْ عِبَادِهِ﴾.
"The Spirit" in this place is prophethood: so that the one upon whom He casts the Spirit may warn of the Day of Meeting. It is called "the Meeting" (al-talāq) only because the people of heaven and the people of earth meet in it.

farraa:16-16.t:
His words: ﴿يَوْمَ هُم بَارِزُونَ﴾.
hum is in the position of a nominative by its predicate after it, and [it is] like your saying: ātīka yawma anta fārighun lī ("I will come to you on the day you are free for me").

farraa:18-18.t:
His words: ﴿ٱلأَزِفَةِ﴾.
It is the Resurrection.
His words: ﴿كَاظِمِينَ﴾.
It is accusative by qaṭʿ (detachment) from the meaning that refers back to them in "the hearts" and "the throats"; the meaning is: when their hearts are at their throats, suppressing [their grief]. If you wish you may make its detachment from the hāʾ in His words "wa-andhirhum"; the first is better in Arabic.
Had it been "kāẓimūna", nominative, on your saying: "when the hearts are at the throats, when they are suppressing", or as a fresh start, it would have been correct.
His words: ﴿مَا لِلظَّالِمِينَ مِنْ حَمِيمٍ وَلاَ شَفِيعٍ يُطَاعُ﴾:
whose intercession is accepted. Then He said: ﴿يَعْلَمُ خَآئِنَةَ ٱلأَعْيُنِ﴾, meaning Allah, Mighty and Majestic. It is said: a man has two glances: the first is permitted to him and the second is forbidden to him. So His words ﴿يعلم خائنة﴾ al-aʿyun refer to the second glance, and "what the breasts conceal" to the first glance. If the first glance was deliberate, there is sin in it too; and if he did not intend it, it is forgiven.

farraa:26-26.t:
His words: ﴿أَوْ أَن يُظْهِرَ فِي ٱلأَرْضِ ٱلْفَسَادَ﴾.
Al-Aʿmash and ʿĀṣim made (al-fasād) nominative, making the verb belong to it [yaẓhara al-fasādu, "that corruption appear"]. The people of Medina and al-Sulamī read: [wa-an] yuẓhira fī al-arḍi al-fasāda, making "corruption" accusative and making yuẓhira [the act] of Moses. The people of Medina drop the first alif, saying: wa-an yuẓhira, and so [it is] in their codices; while in the codices of the people of Iraq: "aw an yaẓhara". [The meaning] is that he said: I fear a change [163/ب] to your religion, or that people will hear [of it] and believe him, so that there will be corruption to your religion in it.

farraa:32-32.t:
His words: ﴿[وَ] يٰقَوْمِ إِنِّيۤ أَخَافُ عَلَيْكُمْ يَوْمَ ٱلتَّنَادِ﴾.
The common people read it al-tanādi, light [without doubling]; al-Ḥasan alone kept the yāʾ [in it]. It is from tanādā al-qawm ("the people called out to one another"). [Abū al-ʿAbbās related to us: Muḥammad related to us:] al-Farrāʾ related to us; he said: Ḥibbān related to me from al-Ajlaḥ, from al-Ḍaḥḥāk ibn Muzāḥim, that he said: The angels will descend from the heavens and surround the regions of the earth, and Hell will be brought; when they see it, it will terrify them, and they will flee (nadda) in the earth as camels flee, but they will not head for any region without seeing angels, so they will return to where they came from. That is His words: ﴿يَا مَعْشَرَ الْجِنِّ والإِنْسِ إِنِ اسْتَطَعْتُمْ أَنْ تنفذوا من أقطار السماواتِ والأرضِ﴾, and that is His words: ﴿وجَاءَ رَبُّكَ وَالْمَلَكُ صَفًّا صَفًّا، وَجِىءَ يَوْمَئِذٍ بِجَهَنَّمَ﴾, and that is His words: ﴿وَيَوْمَ تَشَقَّقُ السَّمَاءُ بِالْغَمَامِ وَنُزِّلَ الْمَلاَئِكَةُ تَنْزِيلاً﴾. Al-Ajlaḥ said: and al-Ḍaḥḥāk read it "al-tanādd" with the dāl doubled. Ḥibbān said: and so al-Kalbī explained it, from Abū Ṣāliḥ, from Ibn ʿAbbās.
Al-Farrāʾ said: And whoever reads it "al-tanād" [light] means the day when the people of Paradise call out to the people of the Fire, and the people of the Fire to the people of Paradise, and the people of the Heights to men whom they recognize.

farraa:35-35.t:
His words: ﴿كَبُرَ مَقْتاً عِندَ ٱللَّهِ﴾.
That is: that disputing is grievous as an object of loathing [tamyīz (specification)]. Similar is: ﴿كَبُرَتْ كَلِمَةً تَخْرُجُ مِنْ أَفْوَاهِهِمْ﴾: in kaburat their saying ﴿اتَّخَذَ اللّهُ وَلَداً﴾ is implied. Whoever makes "word" nominative implies nothing; al-Ḥasan read it so, with "word" nominative: ﴿كَبُرَتْ كَلِمَةٌ تَخْرُجُ﴾.
His words: ﴿عَلَىٰ كُـلِّ قَلْبِ مُتَكَبِّرٍ جَبَّارٍ﴾: He puts "heart" in iḍāfa to "the arrogant one". Whoever uses tanwīn makes the heart itself the arrogant tyrant. In the reading of ʿAbdallāh: "kadhālika yaṭbaʿu Allāhu ʿalā qalbi kulli mutakabbirin jabbārin" ("on the heart of every arrogant tyrant"); this is a witness for whoever reads with iḍāfa. The meaning, whether "heart" comes first or later, is the same, and Allah knows best.
He said: I heard one of the Arabs [say]: "He combs his hair on the day of every Friday", meaning "every Friday day"; and the meaning is the same.

farraa:36-37.t:
His words: ﴿لَّعَـلِّيۤ أَبْلُغُ ٱلأَسْبَابَ (أَسْبَابَ ٱلسَّمَاوَاتِ) فَأَطَّلِعُ﴾.
With the nominative [fa-aṭṭaliʿu], referring it back to His words "ablughu". Whoever makes it an answer to laʿallī makes it accusative [fa-aṭṭaliʿa], and some readers read it so. He said: and one of the Arabs recited to me:
علَّ صروفَ الدَّهر أو دولاتها * يدللنا اللَّمَّةَ من لَمَّاتها * فتستريحَ النفسُ من زَفْراتها *
(Perhaps the turns of fortune or its changes will bring us round to one of its visitations, so that the soul may rest from its sighs.)
He used the accusative as the answer to laʿalla.

farraa:46-46.t:
His words: ﴿ٱلنَّارُ يُعْرَضُونَ عَلَيْهَا﴾.
You make (al-nār) nominative by what refers back to it in ʿalayhā. Had you made it nominative by what makes ﴿سُوءَ الْعَذَاب﴾ (45) nominative [i.e. as a badal (substitute) of it], it would have been correct. And had you made it accusative, on the ground that it falls [164/ا] between something referring back to it and speech connected with what precedes it, it would have been correct. Similar is: ﴿قُلْ أَفَأُنَبِّئكُمْ بِشَرٍّ مِنْ ذَلِكُم النارُ وَعَدهَا﴾.
His words: ﴿غُدُوًّا وَعَشِيًّا﴾.
In the Hereafter there is neither morning nor evening; rather, it is the measures of the evenings and mornings of this world.
His words: ﴿[وَ] يَوْمَ تَقُومُ ٱلسَّاعَةُ أَدْخِلُوۤاْ آلَ فِرْعَوْنَ﴾.
Yaḥyā ibn Waththāb and the people of the Hijaz pronounced the alif with hamza [adkhilū], while ʿĀṣim and al-Ḥasan made it light, reading "wa-yawma taqūmu al-sāʿatu udkhulū āla Firʿawna"; here "the family of Pharaoh" is accusative as a vocative: "Enter, O family of Pharaoh, the severest punishment". In the first case "adkhilū" falls upon them [as its object].

farraa:48-48.t:
His words: ﴿إِنَّا كُلٌّ فِيهَآ﴾.
You make (kull) nominative by fīhā, and do not make it an adjective of innā. And if you made it accusative on that basis [as tawkīd (emphasis)], making [fīhā] the predicate of innā «[Translator's note: the apodosis is missing in the source; presumably "it would be correct"]». Similar is: ﴿قُلْ إِنَّ الأَمْرَ كُلَّهُ لِلّهِ﴾: you make ﴿كلّه لله﴾ nominative, and you make it accusative on this explanation.

farraa:51-51.t:
His words: ﴿وَيَوْمَ يَقُومُ ٱلأَشْهَادُ﴾.
The readers read with yāʾ, meaning yaqūmu in the masculine. Had a reader read "wa-yawma taqūmu", it would have been correct [Translator's note: the source prints «صوبا», a misprint for «صوابا»], because al-ashhād is a plural, and a plural of a masculine may have its verb feminine or masculine when the verb comes first. The Arabs say: dhahabat al-rijāl and dhahaba al-rijāl ("the men went").

farraa:56-56.t:
His words: ﴿إِلاَّ كِبْرٌ مَّـا هُم بِبَالِغِيهِ﴾.
He means: they were too proud to believe in what Muḥammad, Allah bless him, brought; they will not attain that, i.e. they will not obtain what they wanted.

farraa:67-67.t:
His words: ﴿ثُمَّ لِتَكُـونُواْ شُيُوخاً﴾.
In the reading (ḥarf) of ʿAbdallāh: "wa-minkum man yakūnu shuyūkhan" ("and among you are those who become old men"): He made the verb of man singular, then returned to "old men", intending the plural by man. Had He said "shaykhan" (singular), because man is singular in wording, it would have been correct.

farraa:71-71.t:
His words: ﴿إِذِ ٱلأَغْلاَلُ فِيۤ أَعْنَاقِهِمْ وٱلسَّلاَسِلُ﴾.
[You make "the chains" and "the shackles" nominative. And had you made "the chains" accusative and said: "yusḥabūna" (active: yasḥabūna), you would mean] they drag their chains in Hell.
Al-Kalbī mentioned from Abū Ṣāliḥ, from Ibn ʿAbbās, that he said: "[and they] are dragged in the chains". The genitive of "the chains" is not permissible, since the preposition would be implied; but had someone imagining it said: "the meaning is only: when their necks are in the shackles, and in the chains they are dragged", the genitive in "the chains" would be permissible on this approach. Similar, among what was referred back to the meaning, is the poet's saying:
قد سالم الحياتِ منه القدَما * الأُفعوانَ والشُّجاعَ الشجعما
(His foot has made peace with the snakes — the viper and the bold, fierce serpent.)
He made "the serpent" (al-shujāʿ) accusative, while "the snakes" before it are nominative «[Translator's note: the verse as printed in the source vowels الحياتِ with kasra, i.e. accusative]», because the meaning is: his foot made peace with the snakes and they made peace with it; when he needed the rhyme to be accusative, he made the verb of the foot fall upon the snakes.

muyesser-irab:1-1.t: ﴿حم﴾: The discussion of the disjointed letters (al-ḥurūf al-muqaṭṭaʿa) has preceded at the beginning of Sūrat al-Baqara.

muyesser-irab:2-2.t: ﴿تنزيل الكتاب من الله العزيز العليم﴾: ﴿تنزيل الكتاب﴾ is the mubtadaʾ (subject); ﴿من الله﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted khabar (predicate); and ﴿العزيز العليم﴾ are two attributes (ṣifatān).

muyesser-irab:3-3.t:
﴿غافر الذنب وقابل التوب شديد العقاب ذي الطول﴾: attributes of the Divine Name in the previous verse.
﴿لا﴾: the lā of generic negation (lā al-nāfiya li-l-jins).
﴿إله﴾: its ism (noun), indeclinable (mabnī) on fatḥa, in the position of accusative.
﴿إلا﴾: a particle of restriction (ḥaṣr).
﴿هو﴾: a badal (substitute) from the position of لا together with its ism, because their position is nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject); or a badal from the pronoun concealed in the omitted khabar (predicate).
﴿إليه المصير﴾: ﴿إليه﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted, fronted khabar; and ﴿المصير﴾ is a postponed mubtadaʾ.

muyesser-irab:4-4.t:
﴿ما يجادل في آيات الله إلا الذين كفروا﴾: ﴿ما﴾ is negating; ﴿يجادل﴾ is an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ); ﴿في آيات الله﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿يجادل﴾; ﴿إلا﴾ is a particle of restriction (ḥaṣr); ﴿الذين﴾ is the fāʿil (agent); ﴿كفروا﴾ is a past verb, and the wāw is the fāʿil; and the clause ﴿كفروا﴾ is the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun, with no grammatical position.
﴿فلا يغررك تقلبهم في البلاد﴾: the fāʾ is the fāʾ al-faṣīḥa; ﴿لا﴾ is prohibitive (nāhiya); ﴿يغررك﴾ is an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm) by ﴿لا﴾, and the kāf is mafʿūl bihi (direct object); ﴿تقلبهم﴾ is the fāʿil; and ﴿في البلاد﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to ﴿تقلبهم﴾.

muyesser-irab:5-5.t:
﴿كذبت قبلهم قوم نوح والأحزاب من بعدهم﴾: ﴿كذبت﴾ is a past verb, and the tāʾ is for the feminine; ﴿قبلهم﴾ is an adverb (ẓarf), attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial); ﴿قوم نوح﴾ is the fāʿil (agent); ﴿الأحزاب﴾ is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to ﴿قوم نوح﴾; and ﴿من بعدهم﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted ḥāl.
﴿وهمت كل أمة برسولهم ليأخذوه﴾: the wāw is conjunctive; ﴿همت﴾ is conjoined to ﴿كذبت﴾; ﴿كل أمة﴾ is the fāʿil; ﴿برسولهم﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to ﴿همت﴾; the lām is for cause (taʿlīl); ﴿يأخذوه﴾ is an imperfect verb, accusative (manṣūb) by an implied أن after the lām of cause, the wāw is the fāʿil, and the hāʾ is mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the interpreted maṣdar from أن and the verb is genitive by the lām, and the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to ﴿همت﴾.
﴿وجادلوا بالباطل ليدحضوا به الحق فأخذتهم فكيف كان عقاب﴾: the wāw is conjunctive; ﴿جادلوا﴾ is a past verb, and the wāw is the fāʿil, and it is conjoined to ﴿همت﴾; ﴿بالباطل﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted ḥāl, or attached to ﴿جادلوا﴾; ﴿ليدحضوا﴾: the lām is for cause, and ﴿يدحضوا﴾ is an imperfect verb, accusative by an implied أن after the lām; the interpreted maṣdar from أن and the verb is genitive by the lām, and the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to ﴿جادلوا﴾; ﴿به﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to ﴿يدحضوا﴾; ﴿الحق﴾ is mafʿūl bihi; ﴿فأخذتهم﴾ is conjoined to ﴿جادلوا﴾; ﴿فكيف﴾: the fāʾ is conjunctive, and ﴿كيف﴾ is an interrogative noun, in the position of accusative as the fronted khabar (predicate) of كان; and ﴿عقاب﴾ is the ism (noun) of كان, nominative (marfūʿ), the sign of its nominative being an implied (muqaddar) ḍamma on the letter before the omitted yāʾ of the first person.

muyesser-irab:6-6.t: ﴿وكذلك حقت كلمت ربك على الذين كفروا أنهم أصحاب النار﴾: the kāf is a noun meaning "like" (مثل), indeclinable (mabnī) on fatḥa, in the position of accusative as an attribute (ṣifa) of an omitted maṣdar (verbal noun) placed before its governing word; or in the position of nominative as the khabar (predicate) of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject), i.e. "and the matter is like that"; ﴿ذلك﴾: ﴿ذا﴾ is a demonstrative in the position of genitive as muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct), the lām is for distance, and the kāf is a particle of address; ﴿كلمة ربك﴾ is the fāʿil (agent); ﴿على الذين كفروا﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿حقت﴾; and the interpreted maṣdar from ﴿أنهم أصحاب النار﴾ is a nominative badal (substitute) from ﴿كلمة ربك﴾, or in [the position of] accusative by removal of the preposition (manṣūb bi-nazʿ al-khāfiḍ), that preposition being the lām of cause [Translator's note: the source reads «أو في منصوب», apparently a slip for «أو في محل نصب» or «أو منصوب»].

muyesser-irab:7-7.t:
﴿الذين يحملون العرش ومن حوله يسبحون بحمد ربهم ويؤمنون به﴾: ﴿الذين﴾ is the mubtadaʾ (subject); ﴿يحملون﴾ is an imperfect verb, the wāw is the fāʿil (agent), and العرش is mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the clause ﴿يحملون العرش﴾ is the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun, with no grammatical position; ﴿من﴾ is a relative noun in the position of nominative, conjoined to the mubtadaʾ; ﴿حوله﴾ is an adverb (ẓarf), attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted ṣila of ﴿مَن﴾, and the ṣila clause has no grammatical position. ﴿يسبحون﴾ is an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ), and the wāw is the fāʿil; ﴿بحمد﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial), i.e. "accompanied by praise"; ﴿ربهم﴾ is muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); the clause ﴿يسبحون بحمد ربهم﴾ is the khabar (predicate) of ﴿الذين﴾; ﴿يؤمنون﴾ is an imperfect verb, nominative, and the wāw is the fāʿil; ﴿به﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to ﴿يؤمنون﴾; and ﴿يؤمنون﴾ is maʿṭūf (conjoined) to ﴿يسبحون﴾.
﴿ويستغفرون للذين آمنوا ربنا وسعت كل شيء رحمة وعلما﴾: the wāw is conjunctive; ﴿يستغفرون﴾ is an imperfect verb, nominative, and the wāw is the fāʿil; ﴿للذين﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to ﴿يستغفرون﴾; the clause ﴿آمنوا﴾ is the ṣila of the relative noun, with no grammatical position, and it is a past verb, and the wāw is the fāʿil; ﴿ربنا﴾ is the one addressed (munādā), a muḍāf, from which the vocative particle has been omitted, and the vocative clause is the object of an omitted saying, in the position of accusative as a ḥāl, i.e. "saying"; ﴿وسعت﴾ is a past verb, and the tāʾ is the fāʿil; ﴿كل شيء﴾ is mafʿūl bihi; and ﴿رحمة وعلمًا﴾ are two tamyīz (specification) [accusatives], and the tamyīz here is converted from the fāʿil, i.e. "Your mercy encompasses everything, and Your knowledge encompasses everything".
﴿فاغفر للذين تابوا واتبعوا سبيلك﴾: the fāʾ is the fāʾ al-faṣīḥa; ﴿اغفر﴾ is a verb of supplication, and its fāʿil is latent (mustatir), its implied form being "أنت"; ﴿للذين﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to ﴿اغفر﴾; the clause ﴿تابوا﴾ is the ṣila of the relative noun, with no grammatical position; ﴿اتبعوا سبيلك﴾: a past verb, and the wāw is the fāʿil, and سبيلك is mafʿūl bihi; and the clause is conjoined to ﴿للذين تابوا﴾.
﴿وقهم عذاب الجحيم﴾: ﴿قِ﴾ is a verb of supplication, mabnī (indeclinable) on the dropping of the weak letter, and the fāʿil is latent, its implied form being "أنت"; the hāʾ is the first mafʿūl bihi; and ﴿عذاب الجحيم﴾ is the second mafʿūl bihi.

muyesser-irab:8-8.t:
﴿ربنا وأدخلهم جنات عدن التي وعدتهم ومن صلح من آبائهم وأزواجهم وذرياتهم﴾: ﴿ربنا﴾ is the one addressed (munādā), a muḍāf, from which the vocative particle has been omitted; ﴿أدخلهم﴾ is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to what preceded, and ﴿أدخلهم﴾ is a verb of supplication, the fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir), its implied form being "أنت", and the hāʾ is the first mafʿūl bihi (direct object); ﴿جنات عدن﴾ is the second mafʿūl bihi, by extension (ʿalā al-saʿa); ﴿التي﴾ is an attribute (ṣifa); and the clause ﴿وعدتهم﴾ is the ṣila (relative clause) of ﴿التي﴾, with no grammatical position. ﴿مَن﴾ is a relative noun in the position of accusative, conjoined to the object of ﴿أدخلهم﴾ or to the object of ﴿وعدتهم﴾; the clause ﴿صلح﴾ is the ṣila of the relative noun, with no grammatical position; ﴿من آبائهم﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial); and ﴿أزواجهم وذرياتهم﴾ are conjoined to ﴿آبائهم﴾.
﴿إنك أنت العزيز الحكيم﴾: ﴿إن﴾ is an abrogating particle (ḥarf nāsikh), and the kāf is its ism (noun); ﴿أنت﴾ is the mubtadaʾ (subject), and العزيز الحكيم are two predicates (khabarān) of ﴿أنت﴾, and the clause is the khabar of ﴿إنك﴾; or ﴿أنت﴾ is a separating pronoun (ḍamīr faṣl) with no grammatical position, and ﴿العزيز الحكيم﴾ are two predicates of ﴿إن﴾.

muyesser-irab:9-9.t:
﴿وقهم السيئات ومن تق السيئات يومئذ فقد رحمته﴾: the wāw is conjunctive; ﴿قهم﴾ is an imperative verb, and the fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir), its implied form being "أنت"; ﴿هم﴾ is mafʿūl bihi (direct object); ﴿السيئات﴾ is the second mafʿūl bihi; the wāw is conjunctive; ﴿مَن﴾ is a jussive-governing conditional noun in the position of nominative as mubtadaʾ (subject); ﴿تق﴾ is the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ), jussive (majzūm), the sign of its jussive being the dropping of the weak letter; ﴿السيئات﴾ is mafʿūl bihi; ﴿يومئذ﴾: يوم is an adverb of time (ẓarf zamān), attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿تقِ﴾, and إذٍ is a noun, indeclinable (mabnī) on an implied sukūn, because the place is occupied by the tanwīn of compensation, in the position of genitive as muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); the tanwīn compensates for an omitted clause, the implied form being: "on the day when he is taken to account for them". ﴿فقد﴾: the fāʾ links to the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ), and قد is a particle of verification (taḥqīq); ﴿أخزيته﴾ is a past verb, the tāʾ is the fāʿil and the hāʾ is mafʿūl bihi, and the clause has no grammatical position [Translator's note: so in the source; the verse here reads ﴿فقد رحمته﴾, and «أخزيته» appears to be carried over from a similar verse (Āl ʿImrān 3:192); the analysis applies equally to رحمته].
﴿وذلك هو الفوز العظيم﴾: ﴿ذلك﴾ is the mubtadaʾ; ﴿هو﴾ is a second mubtadaʾ; and ﴿الفوز العظيم﴾ are two predicates (khabarān) of ﴿هو﴾; or ﴿هو﴾ is a separating pronoun (ḍamīr faṣl) with no grammatical position, and ﴿الفوز العظيم﴾ are two predicates of ﴿ذلك﴾.

muyesser-irab:10-10.t:
﴿إن الذين كفروا ينادون لمقت الله أكبر من مقتكم أنفسكم﴾: resumptive speech with no grammatical position; ﴿إن﴾ is an abrogating particle (ḥarf nāsikh), and ﴿الذين﴾ is its ism (noun); ﴿كفروا﴾ is a past verb, and the wāw is the fāʿil (agent); the clause ﴿كفروا﴾ is the ṣila (relative clause) of ﴿الذين﴾, with no grammatical position. The clause ﴿ينادون﴾ is the khabar (predicate) of إن; ﴿ينادون﴾ is an imperfect verb, passive, and the wāw is the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent); the lām is the lām of inception (lām al-ibtidāʾ); ﴿مقت الله﴾ is the mubtadaʾ (subject), the annexation being of the maṣdar (verbal noun) to its agent, while the mafʿūl bihi (direct object) is omitted, i.e. "you (إياكم)"; ﴿أكبر﴾ is the khabar; ﴿من مقتكم﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿أكبر﴾; and ﴿أنفسكم﴾ is the object of ﴿مقتكم﴾.
﴿إذ تدعون إلى الإيمان فتكفرون﴾: ﴿إذ﴾ is a noun, indeclinable (mabnī) on sukūn, in the position of accusative as mafʿūl bihi of an omitted verb, its implied form being: "He detested you when you were called", or: "remember when you were called"; the clause ﴿تدعون﴾ is in the position of genitive by annexation; ﴿تدعون﴾ is an imperfect verb, passive, and the wāw is the nāʾib fāʿil; ﴿إلى الإيمان﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to ﴿تدعون﴾; ﴿فتكفرون﴾: the fāʾ is conjunctive, and ﴿تكفرون﴾ is an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ) by the retention of the nūn, and the wāw is the fāʿil.

muyesser-irab:11-11.t: ﴿قالوا ربنا أمتنا اثنتين وأحييتنا اثنتين فاعترفنا بذنوبنا فهل إلى خروج من سبيل﴾: ﴿قالوا﴾ is a past verb, and the wāw is the fāʿil (agent); ﴿ربنا﴾ is the one addressed (munādā), a muḍāf, from which the vocative particle has been omitted; ﴿أمتنا﴾ is a past verb, the tāʾ is the fāʿil, and ﴿نا﴾ is an attached pronoun in the position of accusative as mafʿūl bihi (direct object); ﴿اثنتين﴾ stands in for the mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object), because it is its number; ﴿أحييتنا اثنتين﴾ is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to ﴿أمتنا اثنتين﴾; ﴿اعترفنا﴾ is a past verb, and ﴿نا﴾ is the fāʿil; ﴿بذنوبنا﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿اعترفنا﴾; ﴿فهل﴾: the fāʾ is conjunctive, and ﴿هل﴾ is an interrogative particle; ﴿إلى خروج﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted, fronted khabar (predicate); ﴿من﴾ is a connective (ṣila, i.e. redundant) particle; and ﴿سبيل﴾ is genitive in form and nominative in position, as a postponed mubtadaʾ (subject).

muyesser-irab:12-12.t:
﴿ذلكم بأنه إذا دعي الله وحده كفرتم﴾: ﴿ذلكم﴾ is the mubtadaʾ (subject); ﴿بأنه﴾: the bāʾ is a preposition, ﴿أن﴾ is an abrogating particle (ḥarf nāsikh), and the hāʾ is its ism (noun); ﴿إذا﴾ is an adverb of future time containing the sense of condition; ﴿دعي﴾ is a past verb, passive; ﴿الله﴾ is the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent); the clause ﴿دعي﴾ is in the position of genitive by the adverb being annexed to it; ﴿وحده﴾ is a ḥāl (circumstantial); ﴿كفرتم﴾ is a past verb, and the tāʾ is the fāʿil (agent); the clause ﴿كفرتم﴾ has no grammatical position, because it is the answer of ﴿إذا﴾; the conditional clause and its answer are the khabar (predicate) of ﴿أنه﴾; and the clause ﴿بأنه...﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted khabar of the mubtadaʾ.
﴿وإن يشرك به تؤمنوا﴾: the wāw is conjunctive; ﴿إن﴾ is conditional; ﴿يشرك﴾ is the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ), jussive (majzūm), and it is an imperfect verb, passive; ﴿به﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted [word] that takes the place of the nāʾib fāʿil; and ﴿تؤمنوا﴾ is the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ).
﴿فالحكم لله العلي الكبير﴾: the fāʾ is conjunctive; ﴿الحكم﴾ is the mubtadaʾ; ﴿لله﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to its omitted khabar; and ﴿العلي الكبير﴾ are two attributes (ṣifatān).

muyesser-irab:13-13.t:
﴿هو الذي يريكم آياته وينزل لكم من السماء رزقا﴾: resumptive speech with no grammatical position; ﴿هو﴾ is the mubtadaʾ (subject); ﴿الذي﴾ is the khabar (predicate); ﴿يريكم﴾ is an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ), the fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir), and the kāf is the first mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the clause ﴿يريكم﴾ is the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun, with no grammatical position; ﴿آياته﴾ is mafʿūl bihi, accusative (manṣūb) with kasra; ﴿ينزل﴾ is an imperfect verb, nominative, the fāʿil is latent, and it is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to ﴿يريكم﴾; ﴿لكم﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿ينزل﴾; and ﴿من السماء﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to ﴿ينزل﴾.
﴿وما يتذكر إلا من ينيب﴾: the wāw is conjunctive; ﴿ما﴾ is negating; ﴿يتذكر﴾ is an imperfect verb, nominative; ﴿إلا﴾ is a particle of restriction (ḥaṣr); ﴿مَن﴾ is the fāʿil; ﴿ينيب﴾ is an imperfect verb, nominative, and the fāʿil is latent; and the clause ﴿ينيب﴾ is the ṣila of the relative noun, with no grammatical position.

muyesser-irab:14-14.t: ﴿فادعوا الله مخلصين له الدين ولو كره الكافرون﴾: the fāʾ is the fāʾ al-faṣīḥa; ﴿ادعوا﴾ is an imperative verb, and the wāw is the fāʿil (agent); the Divine Name is mafʿūl bihi (direct object); ﴿مخلصين﴾ is a ḥāl (circumstantial); ﴿له﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿مخلصين﴾; ﴿الدين﴾ is mafʿūl bihi; the wāw is circumstantial (ḥāliyya); ﴿لو﴾ is conditional; ﴿كره الكافرون﴾ is a verb and its fāʿil, and the mafʿūl bihi is omitted, i.e. "your sincerity", or: "your calling [upon Him]".

muyesser-irab:15-15.t: ﴿رفيع الدرجات ذو العرش يلقي الروح من أمره على من يشاء من عباده لينذر يوم التلاق﴾: ﴿رفيع الدرجات﴾ is the khabar (predicate) of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject); ﴿ذو العرش﴾ is a second khabar; ﴿يلقي الروح﴾: an imperfect verb, and the fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir); ﴿الروح﴾ is mafʿūl bihi (direct object), and the clause is a third khabar; ﴿من أمره﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿يلقي﴾, or to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial) from ﴿الروح﴾, i.e. "in the state of its arising from His command"; ﴿على من﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to ﴿يلقي﴾; the clause ﴿يشاء﴾ is the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun, with no grammatical position; ﴿من عباده﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted ḥāl; ﴿لينذر﴾: the lām is for cause (taʿlīl), and ﴿ينذر﴾ is an imperfect verb, accusative (manṣūb) by an implied أن after the lām; the interpreted maṣdar from أن and the verb is genitive by the lām, and the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to ﴿يلقي﴾; the fāʿil is "هو": Allah, or the Spirit (الروح), or whomever He wills; ﴿يوم﴾ is the mafʿūl bihi of ﴿ينذر﴾; and ﴿التلاق﴾ is muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct).

muyesser-irab:16-16.t:
﴿يوم هم بارزون لا يخفى على الله منهم شيء﴾: ﴿يوم﴾ is a badal (substitute) from ﴿يوم التلاق﴾, a badal of the whole for the whole; ﴿هم﴾ is the mubtadaʾ (subject); ﴿بارزون﴾ is the khabar (predicate); the nominal clause is in the position of genitive by the adverb being annexed to it; ﴿لا﴾ is negating; ﴿يخفى﴾ is an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ); ﴿على الله﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿يخفى﴾; ﴿منهم﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial), because it was originally an attribute of ﴿شيء﴾; ﴿شيء﴾ is the fāʿil (agent) of ﴿يخفى﴾; and the clause ﴿لا يخفى ...﴾ is a ḥāl from the pronoun of ﴿بارزون﴾, or a second khabar; and it was said: it is resumptive, with no grammatical position.
﴿لمن الملك اليوم لله الواحد القهار﴾: the clause is the object of an omitted saying, i.e. He the Exalted says it and answers Himself; the saying is conjoined to what precedes it, or it is resumptive, in answer to an implied question, as if it were asked: "So what will happen then?", and it was said: "It will be said: To whom belongs the dominion…?"; ﴿لمن﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted, fronted khabar; ﴿الملك﴾ is a postponed mubtadaʾ; ﴿اليوم﴾ is an adverb (ẓarf), attached to ﴿الملك﴾; ﴿لله﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, its implied form being: "the dominion is Allah's"; and ﴿الواحد القهار﴾ are two naʿts (adjectives) of الله.

muyesser-irab:17-17.t:
﴿اليوم تجزى كل نفس بما كسبت﴾: ﴿اليوم﴾ is an adverb (ẓarf), attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿تجزى﴾, and the speech is a continuation of what is said; ﴿تجزى﴾ is an imperfect verb, passive; ﴿كل نفس﴾ is the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent); ﴿بما﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to ﴿تجزى﴾, and ﴿ما﴾ is relative or adverbial (ẓarfiyya); ﴿كسبت﴾ is a past verb, and the fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir); and the clause ﴿كسبت﴾ is the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun, with no grammatical position.
﴿لا ظلم اليوم إن الله سريع الحساب﴾: ﴿لا﴾ is the lā of generic negation (lā al-nāfiya li-l-jins); ﴿ظلم﴾ is its ism (noun), indeclinable (mabnī) on fatḥa; ﴿اليوم﴾ is an adverb, attached to an omitted khabar (predicate); ﴿إن﴾ is an abrogating particle (ḥarf nāsikh), the Divine Name is its ism, and ﴿سريع الحساب﴾ is its khabar.

muyesser-irab:18-18.t:
﴿وأنذرهم يوم الآزفة إذ القلوب لدى الحناجر كاظمين﴾: the wāw conjoins to what preceded; ﴿أنذرهم﴾ is an imperative verb, and the fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir); ﴿هم﴾ is the first mafʿūl bihi (direct object); ﴿يوم الآزفة﴾ is the second mafʿūl bihi; ﴿إذ﴾ is a noun, indeclinable (mabnī) on sukūn, in the position of accusative as a badal (substitute) from ﴿يوم الآزفة﴾; ﴿القلوب﴾ is the mubtadaʾ (subject); ﴿لدى الحناجر﴾ is an adverb (ẓarf), attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted khabar (predicate), and the clause is in the position of genitive by annexation; ﴿كاظمين﴾ is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from ﴿القلوب﴾.
﴿ما للظالمين من حميم ولا شفيع يطاع﴾: the clause is a ḥāl from the owners of the hearts; ﴿ما﴾ is negating; ﴿للظالمين﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted, fronted khabar; ﴿من﴾ is a connective (ṣila, i.e. redundant) preposition; ﴿حميم﴾ is a postponed mubtadaʾ, nominative in position and genitive in form by ﴿من﴾; ﴿لا شفيع﴾ is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to ﴿حميم﴾; ﴿يطاع﴾ is an imperfect verb, passive, and the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent) is latent; and the clause ﴿يطاع﴾ is an attribute (ṣifa) of ﴿شفيع﴾.

muyesser-irab:19-19.t: ﴿يعلم خائنة الأعين وما تخفي الصدور﴾: the clause is a fourth khabar (predicate) of the omitted mubtadaʾ (subject) whose predicate is ﴿رفيع الدرجات﴾ and what follows it; or it is one of the predicates of ﴿هو الذي يريكم﴾; or it is in the position of accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial); or it is causal (taʿlīliyya), with no grammatical position. ﴿يعلم﴾ is an imperfect verb, and the fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir), its implied form being "هو", i.e. Allah the Exalted; ﴿خائنة الأعين﴾ is mafʿūl bihi (direct object), the annexation having the sense of "من" (of), i.e. "the treacherous among the eyes"; on this view ﴿خائنة﴾ is a naʿt (adjective) of an omitted noun, i.e. "the treacherous eye"; or ﴿خائنة﴾ is a maṣdar (verbal noun), like العاقبة and الكاذبة, i.e. "He knows the treachery of the eyes"; the wāw is a conjunction; ﴿ما﴾ is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to ﴿خائنة الأعين﴾; and the clause ﴿تخفي الصدور﴾ is the ṣila (relative clause) of ﴿ما﴾, with no grammatical position.

muyesser-irab:20-20.t:
﴿والله يقضي بالحق﴾: the wāw is a conjunction; ﴿الله﴾ is the mubtadaʾ (subject); the clause يقضي: an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ), and the fāʿil (agent), its implied form being "هو"; the clause يقضي is the khabar (predicate); ﴿بالحق﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿يقضي﴾, or to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial), i.e. "in accordance with it".
﴿والذين يدعون من دونه لا يقضون بشيء﴾: the wāw is conjunctive; ﴿الذين﴾ is the mubtadaʾ; ﴿يدعون﴾ is an imperfect verb, nominative, and the wāw is the fāʿil; the clause ﴿يدعون﴾ is the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun, with no grammatical position; ﴿من دونه﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to ﴿يدعون﴾; the referent pronoun (ʿāʾid) is omitted, i.e. "they call upon them besides Him", meaning: they worship them; ﴿لا﴾ is negating; ﴿يقضون﴾ is an imperfect verb, and the wāw is the fāʿil; ﴿بشيء﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to ﴿يقضي﴾ [Translator's note: so in the source; the verb in this clause is ﴿يقضون﴾]; and the clause ﴿لا يقضون بشيء﴾ is the khabar of ﴿الذين﴾.
﴿إن الله هو السميع البصير﴾: إن is an abrogating particle (ḥarf nāsikh); ﴿الله﴾ is its ism (noun); ﴿هو﴾ is a mubtadaʾ; ﴿السميع البصير﴾ are two predicates (khabarān) of ﴿هو﴾, and the nominal clause is the khabar of ﴿إن﴾; or ﴿هو﴾ is a separating pronoun (ḍamīr faṣl), and ﴿السميع البصير﴾ are two predicates of ﴿إن﴾.

zajjaj:10-10.t: His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿يُنادَوْنَ لَمَقْتُ اللَّهِ أكْبَرُ مِن مَقْتِكم أنْفُسَكُمْ﴾ — its meaning is: "Those who disbelieved will be called out to, when they are in the state of punishment: Allah's loathing of you in the world, when you were called to faith and you disbelieved, is greater than your loathing of yourselves when you were punished in the Fire."

zajjaj:11-11.t: ﴿قالُوا رَبَّنا أمَتَّنا اثْنَتَيْنِ وأحْيَيْتَنا اثْنَتَيْنِ فاعْتَرَفْنا بِذُنُوبِنا﴾, that is: You have shown us of the signs what necessitates that we must confess. And they said concerning "أمَتَّنا اثْنَتَيْنِ وأحْيَيْتَنا اثْنَتَيْنِ": that is, You created us dead, then You gave us life, then You caused us to die afterwards, then You resurrected us after death. And it has come in some commentaries that one of the two lives and one of the two deaths is that one is brought to life in the grave and then dies; that fits "أحْيَيْتَنا" and "أمَتَّنا" better, but the first is more common in the commentary.

zajjaj:15-15.t: His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿يُلْقِي الرُّوحَ مِن أمْرِهِ عَلى مَن يَشاءُ مِن عِبادِهِ﴾ — it has come in the commentary that "الرُّوح" is revelation; it has come that "الرُّوح" is the Quran; and it has come that "الرُّوح" is the matter of prophethood, so that the meaning would be: "You cast the spirit, or the matter of prophethood, upon whom You will, upon whom You single out for the message". ﴿لِيُنْذِرَ يَوْمَ التَّلاقِ﴾, that is: so that the Prophet ﷺ may warn of the Day of Meeting by what is revealed to him. It is also permissible that it be "so that Allah may warn of the Day of Meeting", but the better — and Allah knows best — is that it be "so that the Prophet ﷺ may warn", and the proof of that is that it has been read: "لِتُنْذِرَ يَوْمَ التَّلاقِ" with the tāʾ. "يَوْمَ التَّلاقِي" with the yāʾ retained is also permissible, and the omission is permissible and good, because it is the end of a verse. The meaning of "التَّلاقِي" is: the day on which the people of the earth and the people of heaven meet. The interpretation of "الرُّوح" in what we have explained is that by it is the life of people, because everyone who is guided is alive and everyone who is astray is like the dead. Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, said: ﴿أمْواتٌ غَيْرُ أحْياءٍ وما يَشْعُرُونَ أيّانَ يُبْعَثُونَ﴾ [al-Naḥl: 21], and He said: ﴿أوَمَن كانَ مَيْتًا فَأحْيَيْناهُ وجَعَلْنا لَهُ نُورًا يَمْشِي بِهِ في النّاسِ﴾ [al-Anʿām: 122]. This is permissible in people's speech: a speaker says to someone who does not understand from him what is for his own good: "You are dead."

zajjaj:18-18.t:
﴿وَأنْذِرْهم يَوْمَ الآزِفَةِ﴾ — the meaning of "أنْذِرْهم" is: make them fear; and "الآزِفَة" is the Day of Resurrection, so it has come in the commentary. It was called "آزِفَة" only because it is near, even if people consider its span far off. One says: "قَدْ أزِفَ الأمْرُ" (the matter has drawn near), when it comes close.
And His saying: ﴿إذِ القُلُوبُ لَدى الحَناجِرِ كاظِمِينَ﴾ — "كاظِمِينَ" is made accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial), and the ḥāl is construed according to the meaning, because hearts are not described as "كاظِمَة" (suppressing [grief]); rather, those who suppress are the owners of the hearts. The meaning is: "when the hearts of people are at the throats while they are suppressing [their grief]". It has come in the commentary that the heart rises from terror and sticks to the throat, so it neither returns to its place nor comes out so that one might find relief from the distress of one's grief. ﴿ما لِلظّالِمِينَ مِن حَمِيمٍ ولا شَفِيعٍ يُطاعُ﴾ — "يُطاعُ" is an attribute of "شَفِيعٍ", that is: "nor any intercessor who is obeyed".

zajjaj:19-19.t: ﴿يَعْلَمُ خائِنَةَ الأعْيُنِ﴾: when a looker looks with a treacherous look, Allah knows it. If he looks a first look without intending treachery, that is not a sin; but if he looks again with the intention of treachery in looking, Allah knows that. Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, is Knower of the unseen and the witnessed, but He mentioned knowledge here so that it would be known that the requital will certainly take place.

zajjaj:23-23.t: His saying, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿وَلَقَدْ أرْسَلْنا مُوسى بِآياتِنا﴾, that is: with Our signs which indicate the soundness of his prophethood — the staff, the bringing out of his hand white without any harm, and the like of that. ﴿وَسُلْطانٍ مُبِينٍ﴾, that is: "a manifest proof".

zajjaj:24-24.t: ﴿إلى فِرْعَوْنَ وهامانَ وقارُونَ﴾ — these names are in the position of the genitive, but they take fatḥa because they are diptotes (mamnūʿ min al-ṣarf), since they are definite and they are foreign. ﴿فَقالُوا ساحِرٌ كَذّابٌ﴾ — the meaning is: "they said: he is a sorcerer, a liar". They made the matter of the signs, which created beings are incapable of, into sorcery.

zajjaj:25-25.t: ﴿فَلَمّا جاءَهم بِالحَقِّ مِن عِنْدِنا قالُوا اقْتُلُوا أبْناءَ الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا مَعَهُ واسْتَحْيُوا نِساءَهُمْ﴾ — it had been said to Pharaoh that his kingdom would cease because of a boy to be born, so it was said: do this, so that the newborn will not escape. ﴿وَما كَيْدُ الكافِرِينَ إلا في ضَلالٍ﴾, that is: it comes to nothing, and Allah brings upon it what He wills.

zajjaj:26-26.t: His saying: ﴿أوْ أنْ يُظْهِرَ في الأرْضِ الفَسادَ﴾ — the codices of the people of Iraq are like this, and in the codex of the people of the Hijaz: "وَأنْ يُظْهِرَ" without alif. "وَأنْ يَظْهَرَ" is also permissible. The meaning of "أوْ" is the occurrence of one of two things; so the meaning with "أوْ" is that Pharaoh said: "I fear that he will change your religion or cause corruption" — he made obedience to Allah the Exalted the corruption — so the meaning would be: "I fear that he will nullify your religion altogether, and if he does not nullify it, he will introduce corruption into it". And whoever reads "وأنْ", the meaning will be: "I fear the nullification of your religion, and the corruption along with it".

zajjaj:28-28.t:
﴿وَقالَ رَجُلٌ مُؤْمِنٌ مِن آلِ فِرْعَوْنَ يَكْتُمُ إيمانَهُ﴾ — it has come in the commentary that this man — I mean the believer of Pharaoh's family — was called "Simʿān", and it was said his name was "Ḥabīb". "مِن آلِ فِرْعَوْنَ" may be an attribute of the man, and "يَكْتُمُ إيمانَهُ" then has something omitted with it, the meaning being: "concealing his faith from them". Or "يَكْتُمُ" may be an attribute of "رَجُلٌ", so that the meaning would be: "and a believing man said, concealing his faith from Pharaoh's family". ﴿أتَقْتُلُونَ رَجُلا أنْ يَقُولَ رَبِّيَ اللَّهُ﴾ — the meaning is: "because he says: my Lord is Allah". ﴿وَقَدْ جاءَكم بِالبَيِّناتِ مِن رَبِّكُمْ﴾, that is: with what indicates his truthfulness among the signs of prophethood. ﴿وَإنْ يَكُ كاذِبًا فَعَلَيْهِ كَذِبُهُ﴾, that is: it will not harm you.
﴿وَإنْ يَكُ صادِقًا يُصِبْكم بَعْضُ الَّذِي يَعِدُكُمْ﴾ — this is one of the subtle questions, because when a prophet ﷺ makes a promise, the promise comes about in its entirety; not part of it comes about. So the question here is: how was it permissible for him to say "بَعْضُ الَّذِي يَعِدُكم" (some of what he promises you), when the proper wording would be "كُلُّ الَّذِي يَعِدُكم" (all of what he promises you)? This is a mode of argument in which the debater goes about establishing the proof with the least of what the matter involves, and there is no denial in this that all of it will strike. Like this is the poet's saying:
قَدْ يُدْرِكُ المُتَأنِّي بَعْضَ حاجَتِهِ ∗∗∗ وقَدْ يَكُونُ مَعَ المُسْتَعْجِلِ الزَّلَلُ
(The patient one may attain some of his need, and with the hasty one there may be slipping.)
He mentioned "some" only to establish "all" for him — not that "some" is "all" — but rather the speaker, when he says: the least that the patient one gets is attaining part of the need, and the least that the hasty one gets is slipping, has made clear the superiority of the patient one over the hasty one in a way the opponent cannot reject. It is as though the believer of Pharaoh's family said to them: "The least that will be, if he is truthful, is that some of what he promises you will strike you, and in some of that is your destruction." This is its interpretation, and Allah knows best.

zajjaj:29-29.t: ﴿يا قَوْمِ لَكُمُ المُلْكُ اليَوْمَ ظاهِرِينَ في الأرْضِ﴾ — this is the report of the saying of the believer of Pharaoh's family. Allah let them know that the kingdom is theirs while they are dominant over all people; then He let them know that Allah's might is not repelled by any repeller, and no helper can help against it, so he said: ﴿فَمَن يَنْصُرُنا مِن بَأْسِ اللَّهِ إنْ جاءَنا﴾

zajjaj:3-3.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿غافِرِ الذَّنْبِ وقابِلِ التَّوْبِ﴾ is in the sense of attributes of Allah. As for the genitive of ﴿شَدِيدِ العِقابِ﴾, it is as a badal (substitute), because it is one of the expressions by which an indefinite noun is described.
And His saying: ﴿ذِي الطَّوْلِ﴾ means "possessor of wealth, bounty and power". You say: "So-and-so has ṭawl over so-and-so" (لِفُلانٍ عَلى فُلانٍ طَوْلٌ), when he has a favour over him.

zajjaj:30-30.t:
﴿مِثْلَ يَوْمِ الأحْزابِ﴾, that is: like the day of party after party. [Translator's note: the printed text reads «يَوْمِ حَزْبِ حِزْبٍ», apparently for «حِزْبٍ حِزْبٍ»; translated as "party after party".] "الأحْزاب" here are the people of Nūḥ, ʿĀd, Thamūd, and those who were destroyed after them and before them.
And the meaning of ﴿مِثْلَ دَأْبِ قَوْمِ نُوحٍ وعادٍ وثَمُودَ﴾ [Ghāfir: 31] is "like the custom of ..."; and it has come in the commentary: "like the state of the people of Nūḥ", that is: "I fear for you that you persist in your disbelief and then there befalls you what befell the former nations who denied their messengers".

zajjaj:32-32.t:
﴿يَوْمَ التَّنادِ﴾ — "التَّنادِ" with kasra on the dāl. Al-Ḥasan read: "يَوْمَ التَّنادِي" with the yāʾ retained, and most readings have "التَّنادِ". Ibn ʿAbbās read: "يَوْمَ التَّنادِّ" with the dāl doubled. The original is "التَّنادِي"; retaining the yāʾ is the proper way, and dropping it is good and fine, because the kasra indicates the yāʾ, and it is the head of a verse, and the endings of these verses are on dāl. The meaning of "يَوْمَ التَّنادِي" is: "the day on which the people of the Garden call out to the people of the Fire: We have found what our Lord promised us to be true; and the people of the Fire call out to the people of the Garden: Pour some water upon us". It is also permissible — and Allah knows best — that "يَوْمَ التَّنادِ" be the day on which every people is called by its leader. Whoever reads "يَوْمَ التَّنادِّ" with the dāl doubled takes it from their saying "نَدَّ فُلانٌ" and "نَدَّ البَعِيرُ" (so-and-so / the camel bolted), when he runs off headlong; and among what indicates this is His saying: ﴿يَوْمَ تُوَلُّونَ مُدْبِرِينَ﴾ [Ghāfir: 33].
And His saying: ﴿يَوْمَ يَفِرُّ المَرْءُ مِن أخِيهِ﴾ [ʿAbasa: 34] ﴿وَأُمِّهِ وأبِيهِ﴾ [ʿAbasa: 35]. And it has come in the commentary that they will be ordered off to the Fire and will flee, and no protector will protect them from the Fire.

zajjaj:34-34.t: ﴿وَلَقَدْ جاءَكم يُوسُفُ مِن قَبْلُ بِالبَيِّناتِ﴾, that is: with the miraculous signs. ﴿حَتّى إذا هَلَكَ قُلْتُمْ لَنْ يَبْعَثَ اللَّهُ مِن بَعْدِهِ رَسُولا﴾, that is: you persisted in your disbelief and thought that He would not renew the obligation of proof upon you. ﴿كَذَلِكَ يُضِلُّ اللَّهُ مَن هو مُسْرِفٌ مُرْتابٌ﴾, that is: like that misguidance, Allah leads astray whoever is a transgressor and a doubter. "مُسْرِفٌ" here is: a disbeliever, and "مُرْتابٌ": one doubting the matter of Allah and His prophets.

zajjaj:35-35.t:
﴿الَّذِينَ يُجادِلُونَ في آياتِ اللَّهِ بِغَيْرِ سُلْطانٍ أتاهُمْ﴾ — "الَّذِينَ" is in the position of the accusative, referring back to "مَن", that is: "thus Allah leads astray those who dispute concerning the signs of Allah without any proof that has come to them". It is also permissible that the position of "الَّذِينَ" be nominative, in the sense: "whoever is a transgressor and a doubter — they are those who dispute".
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿كَبُرَ مَقْتًا عِنْدَ اللَّهِ وعِنْدَ الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا﴾, that is: "their disputing is greatly loathsome with Allah and with those who believe". ﴿كَذَلِكَ يَطْبَعُ اللَّهُ عَلى كُلِّ قَلْبِ مُتَكَبِّرٍ جَبّارٍ﴾ — and it is read: "عَلى كُلِّ قَلْبٍ مُتَكَبِّرٍ" (with tanwīn on قَلْب). The first is the proper way, because the arrogant one is the person; but it is also possible for you to say "قَلْبٌ مُتَكَبِّرٌ" (an arrogant heart), that is, its owner is arrogant.

zajjaj:36-36.t: ﴿وَقالَ فِرْعَوْنُ يا هامانُ ابْنِ لِي صَرْحًا﴾ — "الصَّرْح" is the palace, and every great building is a ṣarḥ. ﴿لَعَلِّي أبْلُغُ الأسْبابَ﴾ — it has come in the commentary: "the gates of heaven". "الأسْباب" in the language is whatever is connected to a thing; and likewise a rope is called "سَبَب", because things are connected by it. It has also come in the commentary: "the ways of the heavens". So the meaning — and Allah knows best — is: "that I may reach what will lead me to the heavens". And "فَأطَّلِعُ" is read with the nominative and the accusative.

zajjaj:37-37.t: ﴿وَإنِّي لأظُنُّهُ كاذِبًا﴾ — this is the saying of Pharaoh. He is saying: even if I claimed that I would look upon the god of Moses, I said this on the basis of Moses's claim, not because I am certain of that. It is related that Hāmān baked bricks for building the tower, and that the first to bake bricks was Hāmān. ﴿وَكَذَلِكَ زُيِّنَ لِفِرْعَوْنَ سُوءُ عَمَلِهِ﴾ — the position of the kāf is accusative; the meaning is: "the evil of his deed was made attractive to Pharaoh" in the way we have described. ﴿وَصُدَّ عَنِ السَّبِيلِ﴾, that is: he was turned away from the straight path — that is, the straight one — by his disbelief. [Translator's note: the source glosses «المُسْتَقِيمِ» with its feminine «المُسْتَقِيمَةِ», since سَبِيل may be masculine or feminine.] ﴿وَما كَيْدُ فِرْعَوْنَ إلا في تَبابٍ﴾: only in loss. One says: "تَبَّتْ يَداهُ", that is: his two hands have lost.

zajjaj:38-38.t:
﴿وَقالَ الَّذِي آمَنَ يا قَوْمِ اتَّبِعُونِ أهْدِكم سَبِيلَ الرَّشادِ﴾, meaning the path of heading straight to Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, and I will bring you out of Pharaoh's path. So "أهْدِكم" is jussive (majzūm), as the answer to the imperative; the meaning is: "if you follow me, I will guide you". ﴿لا جَرَمَ أنَّما تَدْعُونَنِي إلَيْهِ لَيْسَ لَهُ دَعْوَةٌ في الدُّنْيا ولا في الآخِرَةِ﴾ [Ghāfir: 43], meaning that it has no answering of a call in this world nor in the Hereafter. Sībawayh said: I asked al-Khalīl about His saying: ﴿لا جَرَمَ﴾ [Ghāfir: 43], and he said: "لا جَرَمَ" is a rejoinder to [previous] speech, and the meaning is: "it is necessary that the Fire is theirs, and it is true that the Fire is theirs". And he recited:
وَلَقَدْ طَعَنْتُ أبا عُيَيْنَةَ طَعْنَةً ∗∗∗ جَرَمَتْ فَزارَةَ بَعْدَها أنْ يَغْضَبُوا
(I struck Abū ʿUyayna a thrust which, after it, made it due for Fazāra to be angry.)
The meaning is: "it earned them anger and made them deserving of anger". So the meaning of "لا جَرَمَ أنَّما تَدْعُونَنِي إلَيْهِ" is: "it has become necessary that what you call me to has no call", that is: "the nullity of its call has become necessary". ﴿وَأنَّ مَرَدَّنا إلى اللَّهِ﴾ [Ghāfir: 43]: our return to Allah has become necessary; and likewise ﴿وَأنَّ المُسْرِفِينَ هم أصْحابُ النّارِ﴾ [Ghāfir: 43].

zajjaj:4-4.t: His saying, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿ما يُجادِلُ في آياتِ اللَّهِ إلا الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا﴾ — the meaning is: "in repelling the signs of Allah with falsehood, so as to refute the truth with it, ﴿إلا الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا﴾." And the meaning of ﴿فَلا يَغْرُرْكَ تَقَلُّبُهم في البِلادِ﴾ is: let not their safety after their disbelief deceive you, such that they go about as they please, for the end of their disbelief is punishment and destruction.

zajjaj:45-45.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿سُوءُ العَذابِ﴾ ﴿النّارُ يُعْرَضُونَ عَلَيْها﴾ [Ghāfir: 46] — "النّار" is a badal (substitute) from His saying "سُوءُ العَذابِ". It is also permissible that it be nominative by implying an explanation of "سُوءُ العَذابِ", as though someone said: "What is it?", and the answer was: "It is the Fire, to which they are exposed".
If someone says: how are they exposed to it when they are among the people of the Fire? It has come in the commentary that their souls are in the bellies of black birds, exposed to the Fire morning and evening until the Day of Resurrection. Do you not see that after it is ﴿وَيَوْمَ تَقُومُ السّاعَةُ أدْخِلُوا آلَ فِرْعَوْنَ أشَدَّ العَذابِ﴾ [Ghāfir: 46]? And it is read: "اُدْخُلُوا" (enter!), in the sense of a command to them to enter, as though: "and on the day the Hour is established He will say: Enter, O family of Pharaoh, the severest punishment". And it was read: "أدْخِلُوا" (make enter!), as a command to the angels to make them enter the severest punishment.

zajjaj:5-5.t:
Then He made clear how that is, and made known that the nations which denied before them were destroyed, by His saying: ﴿كَذَّبَتْ قَبْلَهم قَوْمُ نُوحٍ والأحْزابُ مِن بَعْدِهِمْ﴾, meaning ʿĀd, Thamūd, the people of Lūṭ, and the nations that were destroyed between these. ﴿وَهَمَّتْ كُلُّ أُمَّةٍ بِرَسُولِهِمْ لِيَأْخُذُوهُ﴾, that is: to gain power over him and kill him. ﴿وَجادَلُوا بِالباطِلِ لِيُدْحِضُوا بِهِ الحَقَّ﴾, that is: to repel the truth with it.
﴿فَأخَذْتُهُمْ﴾, that is: I made their recompense for intending to seize the messengers that I seized them and punished them. ﴿فَكَيْفَ كانَ عِقابِ﴾, that is: they pass by the places in which the peoples were destroyed and see the traces of destruction.

zajjaj:51-51.t: ﴿وَيَوْمَ يَقُومُ الأشْهادُ﴾, that is: the angels. Its singular is "شاهِدٌ", like "صاحِبٌ" and "أصْحابٌ".

zajjaj:56-56.t: ﴿إنَّ الَّذِينَ يُجادِلُونَ في آياتِ اللَّهِ﴾, that is: they dispute in repelling the signs of Allah, without any authority that has come to them, that is: without any proof that has come to them. ﴿إنْ في صُدُورِهِمْ إلا كِبْرٌ ما هم بِبالِغِيهِ﴾, that is: "they will not attain their aim in it", and their aim is repelling the signs of Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He. What indicates this meaning is "يُجادِلُونَ في آياتِ اللَّهِ", because the pride they have already brought about, so this cannot be confused with [meaning] "attaining the pride". And it has come in the commentary that the Jews are meant by it, and that the pride which they will not attain is expecting the matter of the Dajjāl: they were proud, waiting and expecting the emergence of the Dajjāl, so Allah made known that this group which disputes will not live to see the emergence of the Dajjāl. And what supports the saying of whoever said this is the saying of Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, right after this: ﴿فاسْتَعِذْ بِاللَّهِ﴾

zajjaj:6-6.t:
﴿وَكَذَلِكَ حَقَّتْ كَلِمَتُ رَبِّكَ عَلى الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا﴾, that is: and like that the word of your Lord came true, meaning by it His saying: ﴿لأمْلأنَّ جَهَنَّمَ﴾ [Hūd: 119].
﴿أنَّهم أصْحابُ النّارِ﴾ — and "إنَّهُمْ" (with kasra) is also permissible.

zajjaj:60-60.t: His saying, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿سَيَدْخُلُونَ جَهَنَّمَ داخِرِينَ﴾ — its meaning is: humiliated.

zajjaj:7-7.t:
Then He, Majestic and Mighty is He, told of the merit of the believers, saying: ﴿الَّذِينَ يَحْمِلُونَ العَرْشَ ومَن حَوْلَهُ﴾, meaning the angels, ﴿يُسَبِّحُونَ بِحَمْدِ رَبِّهِمْ ويُؤْمِنُونَ بِهِ ويَسْتَغْفِرُونَ لِلَّذِينَ آمَنُوا﴾. So the believer is one for whom the angels brought near seek forgiveness. And it means: ﴿رَبَّنا وسِعْتَ كُلَّ شَيْءٍ رَحْمَةً وعِلْمًا فاغْفِرْ لِلَّذِينَ تابُوا واتَّبَعُوا سَبِيلَكَ﴾ — the meaning is: "they say: Our Lord, You encompass all things", that is, the angels say it.
And His saying: ﴿رَحْمَةً وعِلْمًا﴾ is accusative (manṣūb) as tamyīz (specification). ﴿فاغْفِرْ لِلَّذِينَ تابُوا واتَّبَعُوا سَبِيلَكَ﴾, that is: they kept to the path of guidance to which You called.

zajjaj:71-71.t: His saying: ﴿إذِ الأغْلالُ في أعْناقِهِمْ والسَّلاسِلُ﴾ — this is permissible in three ways: "والسَّلاسِلَ" with the accusative, "والسَّلاسِلِ" with the genitive [and "والسَّلاسِلُ" with the nominative]. Whoever reads the nominative conjoins it to "الأغْلالُ"; whoever reads the genitive, the meaning is: "when the shackles are on their necks and [they are] in the chains"; and whoever reads the accusative, giving fatḥa to the lām, reads: "والسَّلاسِلَ يَسْحَبُونَ" (and the chains they drag). [Translator's note: the source names three ways but lists only two before explaining the third (the nominative); the bracketed words supply it.]

zajjaj:75-75.t: ﴿ذَلِكم بِما كُنْتُمْ تَفْرَحُونَ﴾ (the verse). What indicates it is His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿فَلَمّا جاءَتْهم رُسُلُهم بِالبَيِّناتِ فَرِحُوا بِما عِنْدَهم مِنَ العِلْمِ﴾ [Ghāfir: 83], that is: that punishment which has befallen you is because you used to rejoice in the falsehood you were in. And "تَمْرَحُونَ", that is: you were insolent, exultant and mocking.

zajjaj:78-78.t: ﴿وَلَقَدْ أرْسَلْنا رُسُلا مِن قَبْلِكَ مِنهم مَن قَصَصْنا عَلَيْكَ﴾ — it has come in the commentary that Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, sent eight thousand prophets, four thousand of them from the Children of Israel and four thousand from the rest of mankind. And it has come from ʿAlī, may Allah be pleased with him, that he said — concerning His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿وَمِنهم مَن لَمْ نَقْصُصْ عَلَيْكَ﴾ — "Allah sent a black prophet, and he is among those whose story is not mentioned in the Quran."

zajjaj:79-79.t: His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿اللَّهُ الَّذِي جَعَلَ لَكُمُ الأنْعامَ لِتَرْكَبُوا مِنها ومِنها تَأْكُلُونَ﴾ — "الأنْعام" here are the camels.

zajjaj:8-8.t: His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿وَمَن صَلَحَ مِن آبائِهِمْ وأزْواجِهِمْ وذُرِّيّاتِهِمْ﴾ — "مَن" is in the position of the accusative, conjoined to the hāʾ and mīm (the pronoun "-hum") in His saying: ﴿رَبَّنا وأدْخِلْهم جَنّاتِ عَدْنٍ﴾, that is: "and admit whoever is righteous". It is also valid for it to be conjoined to the hāʾ and mīm in His saying: ﴿وَعَدْتَهُمْ﴾, so that the meaning would be: "You promised them and You promised whoever is righteous among their fathers".

zajjaj:85-85.t: ﴿فَلَمْ يَكُ يَنْفَعُهم إيمانُهم لَمّا رَأوْا بَأْسَنا﴾ — He is saying: "when they saw the punishment with their own eyes". ﴿سُنَّتَ اللَّهِ﴾ is in the sense of: "Allah laid down this practice (sunna) among all the nations: their faith does not benefit them when they see the punishment". ﴿وَخَسِرَ هُنالِكَ الكافِرُونَ﴾, and likewise: ﴿وَخَسِرَ هُنالِكَ المُبْطِلُونَ﴾ [Ghāfir: 78]. "المُبْطِلُونَ" and "الكافِرُونَ" are losers at that time, and at every time they are losers, but He, Exalted is He, made their loss clear to them when they saw the punishment.

zajjaj:1-1.t:
Sūrat al-Muʾmin
﷽
﴿حم﴾ ﴿تَنْـزِيلُ الكِتابِ مِنَ اللَّهِ العَزِيزِ العَلِيمِ﴾ [Ghāfir: 2]: the Ḥawāmīm [the sūras beginning with Ḥā Mīm] are all Meccan, revealed in Mecca. The Prophet ﷺ said: «"The likeness of the Ḥawāmīm in the Qur'an is like that of the ḥibara cloaks (striped Yemeni garments) among clothes."» Ibn Masʿūd said: "The Ḥawāmīm are the brocade of the Qur'an."
It has come in the exegesis from Ibn ʿAbbās, may Allah have mercy on him, that there are three views on "حـم". He said: "(حـم) is the greatest name of Allah"; he said: "(حـم) is an oath"; and he said: "(حـم) are the letters of al-Raḥmān, separated." The meaning is: "الـر", "حـم" and "نُونْ" together are equivalent to "اَلرَّحْمَنُ". We have explained the i'rab of the letters of the alphabet at the beginning of al-Baqara.
The reading of it is of two kinds: "حَـمْ", with fatḥa on the ḥāʾ, and "حِـمْ", with kasra on the ḥāʾ. As for the mīm, it is quiescent (sākin) in the reading of all the readers except ʿĪsā ibn ʿUmar, for he read "حَـمَ والكِتابِ" «[Translator's note: «حم والكتاب» is the opening of al-Zukhruf and al-Dukhān, not of this sūra; translated as written.]», with fatḥa on the mīm. This is of two kinds. One of them is that he makes "حَـمَ" a name of the sūra, so he puts it in the accusative without tanwīn, because it is on the pattern of foreign names such as "هابِيلَ" (Abel) and "قابِيلَ" (Cain), and the meaning is "recite Ḥā Mīm (اُتْلُ حَـمَ)". The better [view] is that he gave it fatḥa because of the meeting of two quiescent letters, where he made it a name of the sūra, and that it is the reproduction (ḥikāya) of letters of the alphabet.
